findings.headline: Chief Internal Auditor role now covers three councils following structural change in April 2026
findings.detail: From 1 April 2026 a single Chief Internal Auditor covers East Dunbartonshire, West Dunbartonshire and Inverclyde. The paper identifies this shared arrangement and other competing priorities as contributing to delayed audit delivery.
findings.matters: The capacity to provide effective audit oversight across three councils from a single person raises questions about audit depth and the council's ability to respond to control issues identified.
findings.quote: there is a new arrangement to share the Chief Internal Auditor with West Dunbartonshire and Inverclyde Councils from 1 April 2026, with a single Chief Internal Auditor covering the three Councils.

findings.headline: Audit completion is 14% of plan at 33% through the year, held back by a vacant Lead Auditor post
findings.detail: The audit team has completed only 3 of 22 planned outputs in the first four months of the financial year, whilst allocating only 13% of budgeted resources. The council identifies the vacant Lead Auditor position as the principal cause of this shortfall.
findings.matters: Under-resourced audit delivery means management control actions are not being properly tested and monitored, increasing the risk that control failures will go undetected.
findings.figures: 3 outputs completed of 22 planned (14%) at 31 July 2026, representing 33% through the year; 13% of resources allocated
findings.quote: The resource constraints as a result of the vacant Lead Auditor post have impacted on the number of outputs delivered by the team.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Treasury Management Strategy Report - 2026-27
findings.headline: HRA financing costs escalate to 40% of net revenue stream by 2028/29, nearly tripling from 14%
findings.detail: The Housing Revenue Account financing cost ratio rises sharply from 14.13% in 2024/25 to 40.26% by 2028/29. This escalation is driven by capital investment peaking at £86.412m in 2027/28, funded by borrowing that lifts HRA debt from £62.683m to £165.638m.
findings.matters: A financing ratio of 40% represents a substantial share of HRA revenue committed to debt service. This signals significant new borrowing for housing investment and raises questions about the council's capacity to sustainably service the debt from its housing revenue base.
findings.figures: HRA financing costs: 14.13% (2024/25) rising to 40.26% (2028/29); HRA debt: £62.683m to £165.638m; HRA capital expenditure peaking at £86.412m (2027/28)

findings.headline: Auditor recommends full reconciliation of fixed asset register due to control failures
findings.detail: Following the discovery of duplicate assets, unapplied revaluations, and inappropriate accruals in the fixed asset register, the auditor explicitly recommended that officers carry out a full reconciliation of the register to the financial statements and valuation report in advance of the 2024/25 accounts to ensure issues do not persist.
findings.matters: A recommendation to perform a full asset register reconciliation suggests the Council's asset records are not reliable without manual intervention. This indicates weakness in the control environment for a material asset class.
findings.quote: We recommend officers carry out a full reconciliation of the fixed assets register to both the financial statements and the valuation report, and perform a thorough review of the fixed asset register in advance of preparing the 2024/25 financial statements to ensure that these issues do not persist.

findings.headline: Council failed to meet statutory deadline for submitting annual accounts
findings.detail: The Council was unable to comply with the Local Authority Accounts (Scotland) Regulations 2014 requirement to submit annual accounts to the auditor by 30 June following the financial year. This represents a breach of statutory obligation and signals process or resource issues in financial reporting.
findings.matters: Timely financial reporting is a core governance requirement. A missed statutory deadline indicates either resource pressures or process breakdowns in the finance function, both of which a lender would want to understand.
findings.quote: The Local Authority Accounts (Scotland) Regulations 2014 state that 'The Annual Accounts must be submitted to the auditor no later than 30th June immediately following the financial year to which the Annual Accounts relate.'. The Council was unable to comply with this statutory obligation
